title: CSV Fields
statement: Implement `solve(text)`. `text` is one CSV line with header `name,note` already known. The line is a data row, not a header. Parse it with the csv module and return `[name, note]`. A quoted comma stays inside the note. Do not split on every comma yourself.
hints: csv.reader on an iterable of one line respects quotes.
Return the two fields as a list.
editorial: str.split on comma breaks a quoted field that contains a comma. The csv module implements those quotes. DictReader is the same parser with headers. This row is positional: the first field is the name and the second is the note.
reference_solution:
def solve(text):
    import csv
    import io
    row = next(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))
    return [row[0], row[1]]
